title: Improve priority routing and burst utilization reporting for Dedicated autoscaler
author: Priya Nandakumar
description:
Context and motivation:
Customers using Dedicated fleets with mixed priority workloads observed repeated latency SLO regressions during short high-QPS bursts. Investigation showed: (1) the autoscaler was smoothing token-bucket allowances globally which allowed low-priority tenants to consume burst capacity; (2) utilization reporting aggregated across priorities so on-call and SRE teams couldn't identify priority-specific pressure.

This PR introduces a priority-aware burst allocation and reporting enhancement for the Dedicated autoscaler. Goals: (a) enforce per-priority burst budgets (token buckets) with smoothing to avoid sudden eviction of high-priority traffic, (b) expose per-priority utilization metrics and dashboards, and (c) add safe rollout controls (feature flag + canary) and migrations for existing fleet configs.

What I changed (high level):
- Autoscaler core (redwood-autoscaler): implement PriorityTokenBucketManager which maintains separate token buckets per priority class and a global throttling guard. Token refill and smoothing logic updated to prioritize higher classes while allowing bounded best-effort burst for lower classes.
- Routing layer (redwood-runtime): add priority-aware routing decision to prefer routes served from protected pools when high-priority tokens are available.
- Metrics and reporting (redwood-observability & redwood-console): add new metrics: dedicated.autoscaler.priority_tokens{priority}, dedicated.autoscaler.burst_consumption{priority}, dedicated.fleet.priority_queue_length and enhanced utilization report endpoints. Wire these into the console dashboard template and update default alert thresholds.
- Config and CLI: bump dedicated autoscaler config schema to v2 (field: priority_burst_policies) with backwards-compatible defaults and add a --autoscaler-priority-rollout flag for canary.
- Tests & perf: unit tests for token bucket math and routing fallbacks, integration test harness for multi-priority workload, and CI perf job that runs a short 1kQPS burst sim to verify latency SLOs for high-priority traffic.
- Docs: update README and ops runbook describing new metrics, how to tune per-priority budgets, and rollback steps.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag defaulted off.
2) Enable on 2 canary fleets for 48h and monitor dedicated.autoscaler.burst_consumption.high and latency SLOs.
3) Gradual enable across regions with short observation windows and automated rollback if alert rates exceed thresholds.

Testing and validation:
- Added 24 new unit tests (token bucket edge cases, smoothing behavior).
- Integration test simulates three priority classes (high/medium/low) and validates high-priority 99th pctl latency stays within SLO under 3x steady-state bursts.
- Ran internal perf harness on staging; high-priority tail latency improved by ~18% under mixed bursts while low-priority tail increased as expected but remained within best-effort thresholds.

Related work and references:
- Linear: ENG-3142 (priority-aware autoscaler), ENG-3160 (observability for Dedicated fleets).
- Previous PRs: builds on ideas from pr-423999 (priority-routing fix) and pr-472500 (burst queueing util reporting fix).

Migration and compatibility notes:
- Default behavior remains unchanged if the feature flag is off.
- Existing fleet configs continue to work; enabling v2 schema on older fleets triggers a safe validation step requiring opt-in.

Callouts for reviewers:
- I would appreciate extra scrutiny on the token refill math (src/autoscaler/token_bucket_manager.go). It affects fairness guarantees and is subtle around concurrent refills.
- Confirm the new metrics cardinality is acceptable for our metric store (we maintain priority as a label with <= 4 values).

Summary: This PR improves burst isolation for high-priority tenants, gives operators per-priority visibility into utilization, and provides a controlled rollout path with fallbacks.
